key_facts: Per the South China Morning Post, China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology approved Alibaba's Tongyi Qianwen (Qwen) models and the Tongyi Wanxiang image and video tool
Apple had received clearance for Apple Intelligence on the Chinese mainland in July but has not rolled it out
Updated filings include network access permits for the iPhone Duo and 18 Pro
iPhone Duo is set to launch in China next week
Engadget notes the SCMP is owned by Alibaba Group
Computerworld says Apple has not discussed its China AI plans
quote_evidence: As reported by the South China Morning Post, which is owned by the Alibaba Group, China's Ministry of Industry and Information Technology has given regulatory approval for Tongyi Qianwen, the group of LLMs better known as Qwen, as well as the Tongyi Wanxiang AI-generated image and video tool.
The company hasn’t yet discussed its plans to bring AI to the Chinese market
why_it_matters_hint: Clears a path for Apple Intelligence on iPhones in China, built on a Chinese partner's models.
notes: SCMP original blocked; read Engadget and Computerworld relaying it. Single-origin report from an Alibaba-owned outlet.
title: China approves Alibaba AI models for use in iPhone Duo and other Apple handsets
